transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Ever since they cut my hours and dumped all this paperwork on me, I just haven’t been handling it well. I feel like I’m reacting all wrong to everything at work, and my sister finally convinced me that I needed to come in and talk to someone.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'reacting all wrong' to things at work, such as feeling anxious, irritable, or overwhelmed?

I'm constantly on edge at work, feeling like I'm on the verge of either snapping or tearing up over the smallest screwups. It's so embarrassing that I've started skipping my rec league games and turning down side jobs with my buddies. I just feel too wound up to handle any of it right now.
You mentioned skipping your rec league games and turning down side jobs, can you tell me more about what specifically makes you want to avoid those activities?

I just feel so wound up and overwhelmed by how poorly I'm handling everything at work right now. I feel like I can't keep up with anything, and I'm too embarrassed to be around my buddies when I'm like this. It's just easier to avoid those activities entirely than to have them see me struggling.
Have you experienced any feelings of detachment from yourself or the world around you, as if you're observing things from outside your body or like you're in a fog?
No, I haven't really felt anything like that. I don't feel detached or like I'm in a fog or looking at myself from the outside. It's more just that I'm extremely stressed out and constantly wound up.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep patterns or appetite since you started feeling overwhelmed at work?
I haven't really noticed any major changes in my sleep or my appetite. Most of my focus has just been on how stressed and on edge I feel during the day.

You mentioned earlier that you don't feel detached, but can you tell me if you've had any experiences where you felt like you were reliving a particularly stressful moment from work, or if you've had any flashbacks to a specific event that's been bothering you?

No, I haven't had any flashbacks or felt like I was reliving a specific moment. My struggle is more about the constant, daily stress of the workload and feeling overwhelmed all the time, rather than re-experiencing a single past event.
Have you been avoiding talking or thinking about your work situation or any specific aspects of it because it feels too distressing or overwhelming?

I don't think I'm avoiding thinking or talking about the work situation—honestly, it feels like I can't stop worrying about it. But I definitely have been avoiding my friends and social stuff because I'm just too wound up to deal with any of it.
Do you feel guilty or ashamed about your reaction to the work situation, or is it more about feeling frustrated and overwhelmed?

It’s really a mix of both. I feel incredibly embarrassed and ashamed of how I’m reacting, which is why I’ve been avoiding my friends and the rec league because I don't want them seeing me so wound up. At the same time, I'm just deeply frustrated and overwhelmed by them cutting my hours and dumping all this paperwork on me without any training.

You mentioned avoiding activities you used to enjoy, like your rec league games and side jobs, but are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or look forward to, or has the stress from work affected your enjoyment of most things?

To be honest, the stress has pretty much ruined my enjoyment of everything right now. I don't really look forward to anything because I'm just too wound up, overwhelmed, and embarrassed about how I'm handling things. I just feel too tired and out of step to find pleasure in any activities at the moment.
Can you tell me more about how long you've been feeling this way since the changes at work happened, and if there was a specific point when your reactions started to feel overwhelming?

This has been going on for about a month now, pretty much since the changes at work and the cut in my hours started to really hit me. All this feeling on edge and not handling things right really kicked in about a week or two after they switched me to all that paperwork stuff. It's just been a constant struggle since then.

Have you experienced any physical symptoms like rapid heartbeat, sweating, or trembling when you feel overwhelmed or on edge, especially in situations related to your work or when you're around others?

No, I haven't really experienced physical stuff like a racing heart, sweating, or trembling. It's more that I just feel extremely wound up and on edge, like I'm constantly on the verge of snapping or tearing up when I get overwhelmed.

Can you describe how your feelings of being 'on edge' and 'wound up' affect your daily functioning at work and in other areas of your life, and are there any specific situations or triggers that make these feelings significantly worse?

My work has slipped so much from being on edge that I actually got a written warning from my foreman, and I’ve completely stopped going to my rec league or doing side jobs because I'm too embarrassed. The feelings get way worse whenever I have to deal with those paperwork tasks I was never trained for, or when my supervisors criticize me over deadlines.
Have you experienced any panic attacks, which are intense episodes of fear or discomfort that reach a peak within minutes, since you started feeling overwhelmed at work?
No, I haven't experienced any panic attacks or sudden, intense episodes of fear like that. I just feel constantly tense and on edge throughout the whole day rather than having it hit me all at once.

Do you find yourself excessively worrying about multiple aspects of your life beyond just your work situation, such as finances, relationships, or health, even when there's no apparent reason to worry?

No, it's not like I'm worrying about random things for no reason. All of this stress is completely tied to the sudden changes at work, my cut hours, and struggling with that paperwork. While it has affected my social life and extra income, it's just because I feel so overwhelmed and embarrassed by these specific work issues.

Can you tell me more about what specifically makes you feel embarrassed or ashamed about your reaction to the work situation, and how this embarrassment contributes to your avoidance of social activities?

It feels shameful because I'm constantly on edge and feel like I'm on the verge of snapping or tearing up over little paperwork mistakes. Since I'm so wound up and embarrassed about not handling these work changes well, I've been avoiding my rec league and side jobs because I just don't want my friends to see me struggling or asking how I'm doing.

Can you tell me if there's a specific aspect of your work situation that you fear or worry about the most, such as fear of failure, fear of being judged, or something else, and how this fear contributes to your feelings of being on edge?

My biggest fear is definitely getting laid off since they already cut my hours, and I have this constant dread of being criticized for the paperwork I was never trained to do. That mix of worrying about my income and feeling completely incompetent at these new tasks is what keeps me constantly on edge and feeling like I'm about to snap.

Have you experienced any significant distress or impairment in your social or occupational functioning that is out of proportion to the severity of the stressor, such as the changes at work, and is this distress causing you significant problems in your daily life?

Yes, this stress has definitely caused major problems in both my work and social life. My performance slipped so much that I actually ended up getting a written warning from my foreman. Socially, I've completely stopped going to my rec league games and am turning down side jobs because I just feel too wound up and embarrassed to face my friends.

Do you feel like your reactions to the work situation and the associated stress are somehow connected to a deeper, more general sense of fear or anxiety that's not just about the specific work issues, or is it really just about coping with these recent changes at work?

It's really just about trying to cope with these sudden changes at work, like the cut hours and all this paperwork. I honestly believe that if they just put me back on regular crew work and things settled down, I wouldn't be feeling like this anymore. It's definitely not some deeper anxiety, just a reaction to this specific job mess.

Can you describe how you would feel if the work situation were to suddenly improve, such as your hours being restored and the paperwork load being reduced, and do you think that would significantly alleviate your current feelings of being on edge and overwhelmed?

Oh, absolutely. If they put me back on regular crew work and cut back the paperwork, I know I'd feel so much better. I really think this level of stress and falling apart wouldn't drag on for more than a few months after things went back to normal.

You mentioned that if your work situation improved, you think you would feel much better and the stress would alleviate; can you elaborate on how quickly you think your feelings of being on edge and overwhelmed would decrease if the work stressors were removed?

I think I'd start feeling better pretty quickly if they just put me back on regular crew work or if things at the company settled down. I really don't think this intense stress and falling apart would drag on for more than a few months after that. It's just this specific situation that has me so messed up.

You've mentioned that your stress is primarily triggered by the changes at work, but can you clarify if there are any other situations or triggers outside of work that also cause you to feel this level of anxiety or being 'on edge', or is it exclusively related to work-related stressors?

It is absolutely exclusive to the work stuff—the cut hours, the paperwork, and the fear of losing my job. While the stress has spilled over into my personal life and made me avoid my friends, those social situations aren't the triggers themselves. Everything really just stems directly from the pressure and changes at my job.

You've emphasized that your stress is almost entirely due to the work changes, but can you confirm if there have been any other significant life events or stressors outside of work that could be contributing to your feelings of being overwhelmed, even if it seems indirect?

No, there really isn't anything else like family drama or other major life events going on. I am stressed about my money because of the cut hours and I feel bad about avoiding my friends, but those problems only started because of the pressure and changes at my job. It all just traces back to work.
Have you experienced any periods where you felt relatively calm and in control, without the overwhelming feelings of being on edge, since the work situation changed?

No, I haven't really had any periods of feeling calm or in control since all these work changes started about a month ago. This feeling of being constantly on edge and wound up is pretty much constant, and it even ruins my free time. It's gotten to the point where it keeps me from doing things I actually enjoy, like my rec league or hanging out with my friends.

You mentioned that your stress and feelings of being on edge are directly related to the work changes, but can you tell me if you've had any similar reactions to significant stressors in the past, or if this is the first time you've felt this overwhelmed by a difficult situation?

No, I've never really felt this overwhelmed or had a reaction like this to stress in the past. Usually, I can roll with the punches, so struggling to keep my head above water like this is a completely new experience for me.

Can you tell me if you think your reaction to the work situation would improve significantly if you were able to find a new job or a different work environment, or do you believe the stress and feelings of being overwhelmed would persist?

Yeah, I think finding a new job or a better work environment where I could just focus on regular crew work would make a huge difference. I really believe that once I'm out of this stressful situation, this level of anxiety and falling apart wouldn't drag on for more than a few months. I just need to get away from all this paperwork and get back to what I'm actually good at.
